Reviewed against the source: the existing quadratic adaptation (square-integer) asks the same thing in the same response form with the source's ranges (x² = a² with a from the source's list 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, 13). Covered as it is.

Reviewed against the source: the existing quadratic adaptation (square-fraction) asks the same thing in the same response form with the source's ranges (b² = a²x² with a from 2 to 10, b from 2 to 9, relatively prime). Covered as it is.

Reviewed against the source: the existing quadratic adaptation (signed-rearranged) asks the same thing in the same response form with the source's ranges (roots −a and −b, a from ±1 to ±9 and b from ±2 to ±9, rearranged with the x² term on the right). Covered as it is.

Reviewed against the source: the existing quadratic adaptation (signed-reversed) asks the same thing in the same response form with the source's ranges (the same roots, written as (a + b)x = −ab − x²). Covered as it is.

Reviewed against the source: the existing quadratic adaptation (negative-roots) asks the same thing in the same response form with the source's ranges (x² + (a + b)x = −ab with a from 1 to 9 and b from 1 to 8). Covered as it is.

Reviewed against the source: the existing quadratic adaptation (scaled-roots) asks the same thing in the same response form with the source's ranges (a common factor 2 to 4, with a repeated root or two roots). Covered as it is.
